documents.name: Edge0
documents.description: Set up Edge0 on Apple Silicon, choose a matching model and understand SSD offload, allocator memory figures and platform limits before testing local inference.
documents.introduction:
## What is Edge0?

[Edge0](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/edge0) is an open-source inference framework for sparse mixture-of-experts language models. It streams expert weights from SSD storage and combines that with trained routing prediction and Recover-LoRA adapters.

The practical aim is to reduce the amount of model data that must remain actively allocated during inference. Storage performance, model files, context length and the rest of the runtime still matter.

This guide follows the official repository and Python instructions checked November 4, 2026. It focuses on selecting the right platform path and verifying a first local run. No inference or speed test was performed for this listing.

## Choose the platform implementation first

The repository has separate Python, macOS, iOS, Android and Windows subprojects. Their existence does not mean every command works unchanged on every platform.

The documented Python framework currently uses MLX on macOS with Apple Silicon. Its CUDA backend remains on the roadmap. Use the platform-specific README for a Windows or mobile build rather than applying the Python installation to an unsupported machine.

The project also describes a future unified inference framework. Treat that roadmap separately from the platform runtimes available in the checked source.

## What does the low-memory figure measure?

The README reports a peak of about 2.9 GiB for the 35B tier and 1.0 GiB for the 8B tier in its short-context benchmark. These are **MLX allocator** measurements, taken with `mlx.core.get_peak_memory()`, rather than total process RSS or a minimum amount of installed RAM.

The reported benchmark machine was a Mac mini M4 Pro with 24 GB memory. File-backed expert pages, runtime overhead, tokenizer data, caches and context growth affect the actual operating picture.

The checkpoints also need disk space: the documentation lists approximately 23 GB for the 35B tier and 4.2 GB for the 8B tier. A small active allocation does not make the model download small.

Use these distinctions when assessing your device. Record total memory behavior and storage conditions during your own workload instead of treating one allocator figure as a device requirement.

## Install the Python framework on a matching Mac

The Python guide requires Python 3.10 or later and recommends 3.12. From a repository checkout:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Edge0-AI/edge0
cd edge0/python
python3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e '.[dev,fetch]'
```

Keep the dependencies specified by the checked project revision. The guide identifies particular MLX and MLX-LM versions; substituting another environment can change compatibility and results.

For a smaller first download, the documented helper can fetch the 8B tier:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/fetch_models.py --tier edge0-8b --target-dir models
```

Each released model directory bundles the checkpoint with its trained LoRA adapters and prerouter weights. Keep the matching files together. A base checkpoint alone is not the complete released pipeline.

## Point the runtime at the actual files

The CLI can accept a model directory directly:

```bash
.venv/bin/edge0 demo models/edge0-8b
.venv/bin/edge0 serve models/edge0-8b
```

Alternatively, the guide documents tier-name resolution through an environment variable pointing to the downloaded directory. Choose one approach and confirm the model location before diagnosing a load failure.

The server exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions route. Compatibility describes its API shape; it does not mean every feature of a particular hosted service is implemented.

Start with a short request and inspect the generated text. Confirm which tier loaded, whether the matching adapters were found and whether output finishes normally before connecting another application.

## Evaluate the workload you actually need

A useful local record includes the repository revision, model tier, adapters, device, storage, prompt length and output limit.

Measure startup, prompt processing and decoding separately. The README distinguishes cold and warm behavior because SSD reads and the operating-system page cache affect the run.

Check output quality on representative requests as well as elapsed time. A faster decode does not establish equivalent task accuracy. The project publishes quality comparisons against its base models, but those upstream results do not replace application-specific evaluation.

The Python guide distinguishes unit tests without real weights from slower real-weight generation checks. Passing the former alone does not demonstrate that a downloaded model can generate correctly.

## License and related tools

The framework repository is Apache-2.0 licensed. Check the model cards and third-party notices for the exact checkpoints and components you use. Local inference also consumes storage, hardware resources and power.

For preparing documents before an AI pipeline, see [Filee](https://findryai.com/item/filee). Browse [Developer Tools](https://findryai.com/category/developer-tools) for related infrastructure projects.

## Official sources

- [Edge0 repository: platforms, model tiers, memory definitions and roadmap](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/edge0)
- [Python framework installation and verification guide](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/edge0/blob/main/python/README.md)

Documentation checked November 4, 2026. All quoted resource figures are upstream measurements or estimates; Findry AI has not independently reproduced them.

reviewedCover.alt: Official Edge0-AI Edge0 GitHub repository showing its streaming MoE inference framework and separate platform implementations.

documents.name: Craft Anything
documents.description: Find ArtCraft Craft Anything's official downloads, understand alpha builder support and inspection modes, then verify a generated project before accepting it.
documents.introduction:
## What is ArtCraft Craft Anything?

[Craft Anything](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything) is an early-alpha ArtCraft application for studying software and building a new project with a coding agent. Its documented workflow moves through studying a target, building, checking the result and refining it.

The project provides a desktop interface, a CLI and an MCP server backed by the same Rust engine. It can also inspect a target without asking an AI to build something.

This guide identifies the official ArtCraft project and explains setup and result verification. It follows the upstream README checked November 4, 2026; it is not a hands-on review or a claim that arbitrary applications can be reproduced accurately.

## Find the official project and release

The authoritative repository is `storytold/craft-anything`, linked from [ArtCraft's product page](https://getartcraft.com/apps/craft-anything). Similar names and third-party download pages do not establish affiliation.

The README links public installers on its [Releases page](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases). Those builds remain alpha. Check the current release notes and platform assets before installing.

For a source build, the checked README requires Rust 1.97 or newer and lists additional Linux desktop dependencies. Its basic commands are:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything
cd craft-anything
cargo run --release -p craft-anything
```

The CLI is a separate install from that checkout:

```bash
cargo install --path apps/craft-anything-cli
craft-anything-cli doctor
```

Use the doctor output to identify missing engines or coding-agent setup before starting a build.

## Separate the app from the builder

The README says building requires a coding agent installed and signed in on your computer. Claude Code is the primary documented builder; Craft Anything launches the user's existing Claude program and sign-in.

Other integrations have different maturity. The checked README describes a Codex adapter as present but not verified on a real installation, and several other agent paths as only partially exercised.

Do not infer equivalent end-to-end support from an adapter appearing in the source. Check the current status documentation for the builder you intend to use.

Questions and analysis can use separately configured providers. The software's open-source license does not include model subscriptions, API usage or optional generation-service credits.

## Choose the inspection mode deliberately

The default Clean room mode works from visible behavior and supplied evidence, such as screenshots, visible text and measured layout. It refuses tools that inspect internal code or files.

Deep mode enables internal inspection tools. Use the target and permissions appropriate to the project you are examining.

The README explicitly distinguishes these tool restrictions from an operating-system sandbox. A coding agent still runs with its own permissions. Review command approvals and the selected workspace before letting a builder change an existing project.

For a first attempt, a small application you own is easier to assess than a large external product. Define which behavior you want to reproduce and which content belongs in the new implementation.

## Start with a bounded project

In the simple interface, select the target type, describe the requested result and review the Study, Build, Check and Ready stages.

Keep the first request concrete: for example, reproduce the layout and one interaction of your own demonstration page at a few screen widths. Ask for your own text and assets.

A project folder records the request and history in `craft.json`, captured evidence in `capture/`, the generated application in `app/`, and comparisons in `checks/`. Existing-folder workflows can edit an application in place or build beside source material; confirm that choice before proceeding.

The CLI also exposes inspection tools and an MCP entry point:

```bash
craft-anything-cli commands
craft-anything-cli mcp
```

Starting an MCP server exposes the engine to a client. It does not itself complete a project or verify the generated output.

## Verify the generated application

The README describes website comparisons at three screen widths. It also marks some app and game behavior checks as partial.

Inspect the produced application directly. Check that it starts, that the main interaction works and that the output folder contains the intended project. Review dependency changes and any failed checks before accepting a Ready label.

For a website, test navigation, form behavior, keyboard access and narrow layouts. For a game, test controls, restart and completion conditions. These are suggested acceptance checks, not results measured for this listing.

A visual similarity report can guide refinement. It does not demonstrate correct server behavior, secure data handling or a successful release.

## Is Craft Anything free?

The repository offers its source under MIT or Apache-2.0 terms. Its checked status section lists a managed tier as future work.

That is different from unlimited free model access. Building uses your configured coding agent, and optional image or 3D generation uses your own service credentials. Check those providers' current terms before budgeting a workflow.

For diagramming a project before building, see [Archify](https://findryai.com/item/archify). For a later interface review, see [Impeccable](https://findryai.com/item/impeccable).

## Official sources

- [Craft Anything README: setup, modes, builders, project files and alpha status](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything)
- [Official ArtCraft product page](https://getartcraft.com/apps/craft-anything)
- [Official releases](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases)

Documentation checked November 4, 2026. No local build, reconstruction or compatibility test was performed for this listing.

reviewedCover.alt: Official storytold Craft Anything GitHub repository showing the ArtCraft software exploration and creation project, source folders and licenses.
